prompt: Steel is galvanised by coating it with zinc to stop it rusting. Even if the coating is scratched and steel is exposed, the zinc still protects the steel. How?

options.text: Zinc paint-like pigment hides the scratch so water cannot find it
Zinc is harder than steel, so the scratch closes up
Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it corrodes preferentially — it is sacrificed while the exposed steel is protected
Zinc makes the steel magnetic, which repels oxygen

explanation: This is sacrificial protection: zinc is more reactive than iron, so when both are exposed and in electrical contact, the zinc oxidises instead of the iron, protecting the steel even at a scratch.
